# Forms

From [the component index](../components.md). A prop with `?` is optional, and `= x` is its default. An indented line is the shape of a value the prop takes. In the examples, `children`, `transactions`, the icons and the handlers stand for the screen's own content, data and state.

## TextField

```tsx
import { TextField } from "@tuja/ui/components/text-field";
```

A one-line text input with its label, help and error.

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<input>`):

- `label: string` — Visible label text. Always required for an accessible name, even when hidden via {@link TextFieldProps.labelHidden} — never rely on a placeholder to name the field.
- `labelHidden?: boolean` — Visually hide the label (kept in the accessibility tree via `sr-only`).
- `description?: string` — Helper text rendered under the label and wired via `aria-describedby`.
- `error?: string` — Error message. When set, the control gets invalid styling + `aria-invalid`, the message renders with `role="alert"`, and it is appended to the control's `aria-describedby`.
- `status?: string` — Live text under the control that follows what the visitor types, such as a preview of what the input will do.
- `size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg" = "md"` — Control height and padding via `controlSize`.
- `look?: "outline" | "ghost" = "outline"` — `"outline"` is the framed box of a form.
- `tone?: "default" | "muted" = "default"` — Colour of the text.
- `leading?: ReactNode` — Decorative leading adornment (icon or unit), rendered `aria-hidden`.
- `trailing?: ReactNode` — Decorative trailing adornment (icon or unit), rendered `aria-hidden`.
- `controlCss?: StyleProp` — StyleX styles merged over the `<input>` itself, such as `typeModifier.numeric` for an amount or a padding for a button laid over it.

Example:

```tsx
function TextFieldExample() {
  return (
    <TextField
      label="Email"
      type="email"
      description="We send the report here."
      error={undefined}
      autoComplete="email"
    />
  );
}
```

## Textarea

```tsx
import { Textarea } from "@tuja/ui/components/textarea";
```

A multi-line text input, optionally growing with its content.

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<textarea>`):

- `label: string` — Visible label text. Always required for an accessible name, even when hidden via {@link TextareaProps.labelHidden} — never rely on a placeholder to name the field.
- `labelHidden?: boolean` — Visually hide the label (kept in the accessibility tree via `sr-only`).
- `description?: string` — Helper text rendered under the label and wired via `aria-describedby`.
- `error?: string` — Error message. When set, the control gets invalid styling + `aria-invalid`, the message renders with `role="alert"`, and it is appended to the control's `aria-describedby`.
- `size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg" = "md"` — Control height and padding via `controlSize`.
- `look?: "outline" | "ghost" = "outline"` — `"outline"` is the framed box of a form.
- `tone?: "default" | "muted" = "default"` — Colour of the text.
- `autoGrow?: boolean = false` — Grow the textarea to fit its content instead of scrolling, disabling the manual resize handle.
- `controlCss?: StyleProp` — StyleX styles merged over the `<textarea>` itself, such as `typeModifier.numeric` for an amount or a padding for a button laid over it.

## Select

```tsx
import { Select } from "@tuja/ui/components/select";
```

One choice from a list of five or more, as a native `<select>`.

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<select>`):

- `children?: ReactNode` — `<option>` or `<optgroup>` elements — the escape hatch when `options` is not enough.
- `label?: string` — Visible text that labels the select.
- `labelHidden?: boolean` — Visually hide the label while keeping it as the accessible name.
- `description?: string` — Supporting copy shown beneath the control and wired via `aria-describedby`.
- `error?: string` — Error message shown beneath the control.
- `options?: ReadonlyArray<SelectOption>` — Config-layer option list; omit it and pass `<option>` `children` instead for the escape hatch (option groups, custom attributes).
  - `SelectOption { value: string; label: string; disabled?: boolean }`
- `placeholder?: string` — Placeholder rendered as a disabled, hidden first option.
- `size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg" = "md"` — Control height and padding via `controlSize`.

Example:

```tsx
function SelectExample() {
  return (
    <Select
      label="Category"
      placeholder="Choose a category"
      options={CATEGORIES}
      defaultValue=""
    />
  );
}
```

## Switch

```tsx
import { Switch } from "@tuja/ui/components/switch";
```

A setting that is on or off and applies at once.

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<input>`):

- `label?: string` — The setting's name. The switch leads and the name follows it, so the two read as one setting with no box around them, at every width.
- `description?: string` — What the setting changes, under the name and aligned with it, wired via `aria-describedby`.
- `value?: "off" | "on" | "indeterminate"` — Controlled state — the parent owns it and must update it via `onChange`.
- `defaultValue?: "off" | "on" | "indeterminate"` — Initial state for an uncontrolled switch.
- `onChange?: (state: SwitchState) => void` — Fires with the next state on every user toggle (pointer, keyboard, label).
- `size?: "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg"` — Track-height scale via `controlHeight`; the width and thumb scale with it.
- `effect?: "liquid" | "none" = "liquid"` — An effect the effect layer draws on the thumb.

Example:

```tsx
function SwitchExample() {
  return (
    <Switch
      label="Spending arrives as a positive amount"
      description="Most banks show purchases as negative."
      defaultValue="off"
    />
  );
}
```

## Checkbox

```tsx
import { Checkbox } from "@tuja/ui/components/checkbox";
```

A yes or no in a form that is saved later, or one pick of many.

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<input>`):

- `label: string` — Visible text that labels the checkbox.
- `labelHidden?: boolean` — Visually hide the label while keeping it as the accessible name.
- `description?: string` — Supporting copy under the label and aligned with it, wired via `aria-describedby`.
- `error?: string` — Error message shown beneath the label.
- `indeterminate?: boolean` — Renders the mixed/partial ("dash") state.
- `size?: "sm" | "md" = "md"` — Box and type scale.
- `look?: "done" | "selection"` — What the tick means.
- `readOnly?: boolean = false` — Shows the state with no way to change it, as in a preview: a muted tick when checked, a muted dot when not, and no box.

Example:

```tsx
function CheckboxExample() {
  const [paused, setPaused] = useState(false);
  return (
    <Checkbox
      label="Paused"
      description="A paused rule adds nothing until you resume it."
      checked={paused}
      onChange={(event) => {
        setPaused(event.target.checked);
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

## SegmentedControl

```tsx
import { SegmentedControl } from "@tuja/ui/components/segmented-control";
```

One of two to four views or kinds, such as Expense and Income.

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<div>`):

- `options: readonly SegmentedControlOption<TValue>[]` — Ordered segments. Arrow-key navigation follows this order; each icon is decorative.
  - `SegmentedControlOption { value: TValue; label: ReactNode; icon?: ReactNode; selectedIcon?: ReactNode; aria-label?: string }`
- `value: TValue` — The selected value. Must match one of `options`.
- `onChange: (next: TValue) => void` — Called with the next value on click, drag or keyboard select.
- `size?: "sm" | "md" = "md"` — Height and type scale.
- `fullWidth?: boolean` — Stretches the track to fill its container, sharing width equally between segments.
- `hideLabels?: boolean` — Collapses every segment to its icon, for a tight bar.
- `effect?: "liquid" | "none" = "liquid"` — An effect the effect layer draws on the indicator.
- `aria-label?: string` — Names the radiogroup. Required unless `aria-labelledby` is given — the segment labels name the options, never the group.
- `aria-labelledby?: string` — Id of a visible element that names the group.

Example:

```tsx
function SegmentedControlExample() {
  const [kind, setKind] = useState<"expense" | "income">("expense");
  return (
    <SegmentedControl
      aria-label="Kind"
      options={[
        { value: "expense", label: "Expense" },
        { value: "income", label: "Income" },
      ]}
      value={kind}
      onChange={setKind}
    />
  );
}
```

## FilterChips

```tsx
import { FilterChips } from "@tuja/ui/components/filter-chips";
```

One filter of a list among any number that all show, such as All, Filed, Archived, Junk, with an optional count each; a row too wide scrolls sideways.

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<div>`):

- `options: readonly FilterChipsOption<TValue>[]` — The chips in order.
  - `FilterChipsOption { value: TValue; label: ReactNode; count?: number; countIntent?: "neutral" | "danger"; aria-label?: string }`
- `value: TValue` — The selected value. Must match one of `options`.
- `onChange: (next: TValue) => void` — Called with the next value on a click or an arrow key.
- `size?: "xs" | "sm" = "sm"` — Height and type scale, the same steps as an outline `Button`.
- `scrollButtons?: { startLabel: string; endLabel: string }` — The accessible names of the buttons that scroll the row one page towards each end.
- `aria-label?: string` — Names the group, such as "Show".
- `aria-labelledby?: string` — The id of a visible element that names the group.

## RadioGroup

```tsx
import { RadioGroup } from "@tuja/ui/components/radio-group";
```

One of a few plain answers, each a radio with a label and an optional description, such as when to notify.

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<div>`):

- `aria-label?: string` — Names the group. Required unless `aria-labelledby` is given, because the labels name the options, never the group.
- `aria-labelledby?: string` — The id of a visible element that names the group, usually the question above it, such as a `CardTitle`.
- `options: readonly RadioGroupOption<TValue>[]` — The options in order.
  - `RadioGroupOption { value: TValue; label: ReactNode; description?: ReactNode; disabled?: boolean }`
- `name?: string` — The name that the radios share, under which a form sends the picked value.
- `value?: TValue` — The picked value, for a group that the parent controls.
- `defaultValue?: TValue` — The value picked at first, for a group that keeps its own state, such as one that a form reads when it is sent.
- `onChange?: (next: TValue) => void` — Called with the value the visitor picks.

## OptionCardGroup, OptionCard, OptionCardStack

```tsx
import { OptionCardGroup } from "@tuja/ui/components/option-card-group";
import { OptionCard } from "@tuja/ui/components/option-card";
import { OptionCardStack } from "@tuja/ui/components/option-card-stack";
```

A choice where each answer needs a description, such as a plan; render `OptionCard`s yourself in an `OptionCardStack` for custom content.

### OptionCardGroup

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<div>`):

- `options: readonly OptionCardGroupOption<TValue>[]` — Ordered cards. Arrow-key navigation follows this order, and a disabled card is skipped by it.
  - `OptionCardGroupOption { value: TValue; label: ReactNode; description?: ReactNode; icon?: ReactNode; disabled?: boolean }`
- `look?: "row" | "tile"` — A stack of full-width rows, or a grid of centred tiles that wraps at 9rem per card.
- `descriptionLines?: 1 | 2` — Makes every card the same height: the label truncates to one line, and the description clamps to this many lines and keeps their height when it is shorter.
- `aria-label?: string` — Names the group. Required unless `aria-labelledby` is given — one of the two is enforced at the type level, because the card labels name the options, never the group.
- `aria-labelledby?: string` — Id of a visible element that names the group — usually the question above it.
- `selection?: "single" | "multiple"` — Single renders a radiogroup with roving focus; multiple renders a plain group of independently tabbable checkboxes.
- `value: TValue | readonly TValue[]` — The selected value, or the selected values when `selection` is `"multiple"`.
- `onChange: ((next: TValue) => void) | ((next: TValue[]) => void)` — Called with the next value on click or keyboard select; with the next array whenever a multi-select card is toggled.

### OptionCard

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<button>`):

- `children?: ReactNode` — Bespoke content under the description — the escape hatch to the custom layer.
- `label: ReactNode` — The card's primary text, and its accessible name on its own — nothing else in the card joins the name.
- `description?: ReactNode` — Supporting copy beneath the label, attached as the card's description via `aria-describedby`.
- `icon?: ReactNode` — Decorative leading graphic, rendered `aria-hidden`.
- `indicator?: ReactNode` — Replaces the selection indicator, which defaults to a radio dot or a checkbox tick following `role`.
- `selected?: boolean` — Whether the card is chosen.
- `look?: "row" | "tile" = "row"` — A full-width row, or a centred tile for a grid of small cards.
- `role?: "radio" | "checkbox"` — Selection semantics, and the difference a screen reader hears: a radio announces "one of N", a checkbox "on/off".

### OptionCardStack

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<div>`):

- `look?: "row" | "tile" = "row"` — A stack of full-width rows, or a grid of centred tiles that wraps at 9rem per card.
- `descriptionLines?: 1 | 2` — Makes every card the same height: the label truncates to one line, and the description clamps to this many lines and keeps their height when it is shorter.

Example:

```tsx
function OptionCardGroupExample() {
  const [plan, setPlan] = useState<"free" | "pro">("pro");
  return (
    <OptionCardGroup
      aria-label="Plan"
      options={[
        { value: "free", label: "Free", description: "One project." },
        {
          value: "pro",
          label: "Pro",
          description: "Every project, and support.",
        },
      ]}
      value={plan}
      onChange={setPlan}
    />
  );
}
```

## Slider

```tsx
import { Slider } from "@tuja/ui/components/slider";
```

A number in a range, picked by dragging.

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<input>`):

- `label: string` — Visible label text, and the control's accessible name — it lands on the `<input>` itself via `htmlFor`, never on a wrapper.
- `labelHidden?: boolean` — Visually hide the label (kept in the accessibility tree via `sr-only`).
- `description?: string` — Helper text rendered under the label and wired via `aria-describedby`.
- `error?: string` — Error message. Turns the track danger-coloured, sets `aria-invalid`, renders with `role="alert"`, and joins `aria-describedby`.
- `readout?: ReactNode` — Live value display rendered opposite the label.
- `min?: number = 0` — Lower bound of the range, and where an uncontrolled Slider with no `defaultValue` starts.
- `max?: number = 100` — Upper bound of the range.
- `step?: number = 1` — Granularity of each step, for the pointer and for the arrow keys alike.
- `onCommit?: (value: number) => void` — Fires once when an interaction that moved the value ends — pointer release, key release, or losing focus mid-gesture.
- `size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg" = "md"` — Track height and thumb diameter, both driven by `controlSize`.
- `value?: number` — Controlled value. Requires `onChange` — without it, the thumb springs back to its current value the moment it is released.
- `onChange?: (value: number) => void` — Fires with the next number on every value change, including each move of a drag.
- `defaultValue?: number = min` — Starting value for an uncontrolled Slider.
